text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service="inference-serving-prod" (PD-12345). Severity: critical. Trigger: 95th latency > 3s, error-rate spike ~5%. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-12345 

pagerduty: AUTOMATED: Incident PD-12345 created and routed to on-call. Escalation policy: inference-prod -> platform-sre.

aj: oncall here, acking PD now. I'll start triage. Anyone seen a deploy? :eyes:

kevin_platform: no recent deploys in the last 30m from CI. I see a flurry of requests to /v1/generate and several 500s from the runtime.

jules_support: getting inbound tickets — customers reporting timeouts and 500s. Support triage shows 10+ customer-impacting requests in last 5m.

aj: ok. first things: (1) confirm health of worker pool (2) check model runner logs for OOMs / exceptions (3) check autoscaler.

erin_sre: i'll pull pod logs and metrics. grabbing `kubectl` now.

aj: paste outputs here if helpful. Also please check the batching queue length metric: `inference.request_queue_length`

kevin_platform: here are some quicks:
```
# kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=inference-runner
NAME                                      READY  STATUS   RESTARTS  AGE
runner-rtx-0                              1/1    Running  0         12d
runner-rtx-1                              0/1    CrashLoopBackOff 4   2m
runner-rtx-2                              1/1    Running  0         12d
```
Logs from runner-rtx-1:
```
E 2026-05-02T14:12:05Z runtime.cpp:432 assert: KVCache::alloc failed: out of memory
E 2026-05-02T14:12:05Z model_runner.cpp:215 runtime exception: allocation failed
```
```
metrics snapshot:
inference.95th_latency_ms = 3200
inference.error_rate = 0.058
inference.request_queue_length = 420
```

aj: KV cache OOM on runner-rtx-1; queue backing up -> latency spike. Could be memory leak or sudden traffic burst.

maria_pm: customers impacted: ACME (support-40123), BetaApps (support-40125). Both report 30-60s timeouts. We're coordinating status page.

jules_support: I opened incident tickets for both and notified account teams. ETA messaging drafted.

erin_sre: I'm going to isolate the failing pod and restart the replica set to get more capacity. Also increasing target replicas from 3 -> 5 as short-term mitigation.

kevin_platform: rolling scale up now via k8s HPA override. command:
```
kubectl scale deployment inference-runner --replicas=5 -n inference
```

aj: good. I'm going to pause autoscaler to avoid flip-flopping while we stabilize.

pagerduty: PD-12345 acknowledged by aj. Notifying escalation contacts.

(5m later)

erin_sre: after scale, queue length down to ~80, 95th latency 900ms, error_rate 1.2%. Some pods still evicting KV caches frequently but overall throughput improving.

aj: nice. keep monitoring. kevin, any idea why KV cache exhausted? memory leak or model input sizes?

kevin_platform: preliminary logs show a sudden increase in concurrent long-context requests (many with 16k tokens). That increases KV per-request and spikes memory. Also one worker reported repeated `cudaOutOfMemoryError` before OOM. Might be combo of traffic pattern + less headroom due to recent runtime memory regressions.

erin_sre: created temp alert to watch `inference.kv_cache_evictions` and `cuda.OOM.count`.

maria_pm: notifying impacted customers with status update: "we're experiencing elevated latency and 500s for generation requests; mitigation underway". Getting CS signoff now.

jules_support: status page updated.

aj: decision tree here: (A) scale up capacity (done) (B) roll back recent runtime change if evidence of regression (C) implement rate-limiting / circuit-breakers for large context requests to protect pool. For now we continue with (A) + live monitoring.

kevin_platform: i'm digging on recent runtime changes. There's one PR that adjusted KV cache allocation heuristics two days ago. Rolling back to previous image could be prudent if we see repeated OOMs across nodes.

(20m after start)

erin_sre: traffic steady. queue ~45, 95th latency 700ms, error_rate 0.8%. I recommend holding for 30 more minutes and then plan for controlled rollback if OOMs persist.

aj: agreed. i'm handing off ownership to erin_sre for the next hour to monitor and coordinate with platform. I'm going to rotate off — pairing with on-call backup. Thanks.

aj: handing off to @erin_sre — please post updates to this thread and ping PD if we need escalation.

erin_sre: taking over (oncall). I'll continue to monitor and liaise with platform. If error_rate goes above 2% or queue > 200, i'll re-escalate.

pagerduty: note: PD-12345 is assigned to aj, now noted as delegated to erin_sre.

kevin_platform: i've queued a rollback candidate to the previous runtime image (image: registry/redwood/runtime:v2026-04-28). Holding off until we have stable repro.

maria_pm: preparing post-incident communication draft. Will include timeline and mitigation steps once resolved.

(45m after start)

erin_sre: All green for now. No further OOMs. Rolling back not required. Running additional load-tests to validate.

jules_support: Support tickets updated; customers acknowledged the status update and appreciate the quick mitigation.

aj: thanks everyone. I'll close my PD ack if team comfortable.

erin_sre: i'll keep PD open until we hit a 60-minute stable window. Assigning follow-ups: platform to investigate KV cache heuristics (kevin_platform), runtime team to add OOM detection & auto-mitigation (sre squad), PM to finalize customer comms (maria_pm).

pagerduty: PD-12345 status: monitoring (acked by aj, assigned to erin_sre).

(incident closed summary posted later)
erin_sre: Incident update: PD-12345 resolved at 2026-05-02T15:05:00Z. Root cause: transient surge of very long-context requests plus reduced memory headroom after heuristic change; resulted in KV cache allocation failures on a subset of nodes. Mitigation: scaled up replicas and paused autoscaler to absorb surge; rollback not required. Next steps: runtime team to harden KV alloc, add OOM alerting and quota-based throttling for extremely large contexts. Postmortem scheduled 2026-05-04 10:00 UTC.

maria_pm: customer comms sent.

jules_support: closing customer tickets after confirmation.

aj: closing my PD ack. Good job team. :tada:
